body.zh-HK:
> 面試官問：「設計一個內部政策 assistant，文件有角色權限，例外個案要交回人手。你由哪一句開始？」
>
> 答啱一半嘅答案：「我會用 RAG、agent、monitoring 和 Kubernetes。」

這些元件可能最後會出現，但一開始列清單會掩蓋真正要設計的決定。先問：哪位 staff 在哪個情況需要知道甚麼、錯答會令甚麼決定變壞、哪些問題系統必須拒絕、誰擁有政策真相和例外。答案由這張 problem brief 長出來，才會知道是否需要 RAG、哪種 permission filter 和何時不應生成結論。

## 由一個受限決定開始

假設 scope 只係幫已登入的 staff 找到現行政策段落並草擬一個附引用的 internal reply。它不改訂單、不聯絡客戶、不覆蓋 policy owner 的決定。Success 不叫『回答率』，而是：在一組固定、已授權的 synthetic requests 上，staff 能否看見合適版本、清楚知道資料不足／有衝突時要交畀誰、以及系統有否保留不該看到的資料。先用 keyword search 或 FAQ 做 baseline，因為你要知道 RAG 是否真的帶來可檢查的增益。

## 架構要對應一條失敗路徑

Ingestion 需要 source receipt、版本、effective date 和 owner；access layer 在 retrieval 前按 role、tenant、purpose 和有效期 filter；retrieval 留 candidate IDs；generation 要引用 passage；output gate 檢查 citation 是否支持、資料是否衝突、是否要 handoff。每一層都回答同一條問題：它防甚麼失敗、如何測、失敗時系統去邊。若兩份文件矛盾，model 不可以平均成第三條規則；它要帶出衝突與 owner。

## 先設三種不能發生的事

例如：未授權文件不進 candidate set；過期／矛盾 source 不被包裝成確定答案；例外 request 不會被自動批准。把它們寫成 fixtures 和 route assertions，不是只放進 prompt。再加入正常 case、無結果 case、角色不同但 wording 相同的 case、文檔更新 case 和 ambiguous exception。每條有 expected document、reply style、handoff 或 refusal。這使 system design 能被 review，而非靠架構圖的箭咀。

## 面試時由選擇講到代價

你可以答：『我由 staff 的決定和 non-goal 開始，先留一個可用的 search baseline。任何生成都只在 permission-filtered、versioned source 上工作；衝突、缺 source 和例外都有 owner 和 handoff。』然後補一個 trade-off：更嚴的 access filter 可能令 answer rate 降低，卻避免資料越權；多一個 handoff 會慢，但比 model 靜靜創作政策安全。

## 作品集裡可以打開的證據

- **工程：** one-page problem brief、source receipt、permission matrix、fixture suite、retrieval／citation trace、baseline/candidate comparison。
- **交付：** staff 使用範圍、policy owner、例外 route、資料更新責任、明確的 non-goal 和停用條件。
- **風險：** 一個得分流暢但被拒絕的回答，因為來源過期、資料衝突或 user 沒有權限。

## 延伸閱讀

[RAG、retrieval、generation 還是 permission 出錯？](/zh-HK/interview-lab/rag-retrieval-generation-or-permission)、[來源互相矛盾時，要有 owner](/zh-HK/interview-lab/conflicting-sources-need-an-owner)、[PolicyPilot 旗艦案例](/zh-HK/articles/enterprise-ai-portfolio-policy-pilot) 和 [RAG portfolio evidence](/zh-HK/articles/rag-chatbot-to-portfolio-evidence)。

## 範圍說明

這是 AI.DOG 的單題練習。staff、policy、權限、source 和 artefact 均為 synthetic 教學材料；它不描述公司內部系統、真實政策或現時招聘流程。

body.en:
> Interviewer asks: “Design an internal policy assistant with document permissions and human escalation for exceptions. What is your first sentence?”
>
> Half-right answer: “I would use RAG, agents, monitoring and Kubernetes.”

Those components may appear eventually, but listing them first hides the decision that needs designing. Ask instead: which staff member needs to know what in which situation, which decision gets worse when the answer is wrong, which questions must be refused, and who owns policy truth and exceptions? That problem brief tells you whether RAG is needed, what permission filter is required, and when a conclusion should not be generated.

## Begin with a bounded decision

Assume the scope is limited to helping an authenticated staff member find a current policy passage and draft an internal reply with citations. It does not change an order, contact a customer, or override a policy owner. Success is not ‘answer rate’. On fixed authorised synthetic requests, can staff see an appropriate version, understand who owns an insufficiency or conflict, and avoid seeing data they should not? Start with keyword search or an FAQ as a baseline, because you need to know whether RAG creates an inspectable gain.

## Every component should answer to a failure path

Ingestion needs a source receipt, version, effective date and owner. An access layer filters by role, tenant, purpose and validity before retrieval. Retrieval retains candidate IDs. Generation cites passages. An output gate checks support, conflicts and handoff. Every layer answers the same question: which failure does it prevent, how is it tested, and where does the system go when it fails? If two documents conflict, the model cannot average them into a third rule; it surfaces the conflict and owner.

## Name three things that must not happen

For example: unauthorised material never enters the candidate set; expired or conflicting source is not packaged as a certain answer; an exception request is not auto-approved. Write these as fixtures and route assertions, not only prompt text. Add normal, no-result, role-different/same-wording, document-update and ambiguous-exception cases. Each has an expected document, reply style, handoff or refusal. That makes the design reviewable rather than an architecture diagram with arrows.

## Move from choice to cost in the interview

You can say: ‘I begin with the staff decision and non-goal, retaining a useful search baseline. Generation operates only on permission-filtered, versioned sources; conflicts, missing sources and exceptions each have an owner and handoff.’ Then name a trade-off: stricter access filtering may lower answer rate but prevents overreach; another handoff slows the process but is safer than a model quietly inventing policy.

## Evidence that belongs in a portfolio

- **Engineering:** a one-page problem brief, source receipt, permission matrix, fixture suite, retrieval/citation trace and baseline/candidate comparison.
- **Delivery:** staff-use scope, policy owner, exception route, data-update responsibility, explicit non-goals and a disable condition.
- **Risk:** a fluent result rejected because its source is expired, conflicted or unavailable to that user.

## Further reading

[RAG, retrieval, generation or permission?](/en/interview-lab/rag-retrieval-generation-or-permission), [Conflicting sources need an owner](/en/interview-lab/conflicting-sources-need-an-owner), [The PolicyPilot flagship case](/en/articles/enterprise-ai-portfolio-policy-pilot), and [RAG portfolio evidence](/en/articles/rag-chatbot-to-portfolio-evidence).

## Scope note

This is an AI.DOG single-question practice exercise. Staff, policies, permissions, sources and artefacts are synthetic teaching material; they do not describe a company internal system, real policy, or current hiring process.
